title: Development of an NMR spectroscopy-based screening method for evaluating lipid profiles in serum and metabolites in urine to assess cardiovascular risk and enable early detection of type 2 diabetes in MASLD patients
summary: The clinical picture examined is metabolically associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly known as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. This is a chronic liver disease associated with increased accumulation of fat in the liver cells and the presence of at least one metabolic risk factor (e.g., obesity, high blood pressure, lipid metabolism disorder, type 2 diabetes). Many patients with fatty liver disease have type 2 diabetes or develop it as the disease progresses. This increases the risk of fatty liver disease progressing and chronic inflammation developing. Patients with MASLD often have an increased risk of high blood lipid levels and therefore also an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. In this study, we want to find out whether specific blood tests (measurement of a profile (type and size) of blood lipids using NMR/nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (Nuclear Magnetic Resonance) and urine (measuring the concentration of various metabolites) can be used to assess the risk of cardiovascular disease (diseases of the heart and blood vessels, e.g., high blood pressure, arteriosclerosis (hardening of the arteries), coronary heart disease (often leading to heart attack), heart failure, and stroke) and the development of type 2 diabetes. The results of the study may support the early detection of diseases and the development of new therapeutic and preventive approaches.
conditions: Fatty (change of) liver, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name: Patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) without diabetes type 2

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Male and female participants aged between 18 and 75, evidence of fatty liver disease (with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus)
Exclusion criteria:
-Refusal of consent
-Pregnancy
-Malignant diseases currently active and in the past 5 years
-Any chronic inflammatory bowel disease (e.g., Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis)
-Active infectious diseases, especially of the liver
